checks: Checked 98a6372650bd3579 main theorem and its parity consequence for A equal to the whole space, and 668ad0ef7a63372e §1 for the relative domain A equal to the projection of C. Both apply to chosen exclusive witnesses and provide the stated argument.

Full dimensionality makes each witness tight on its own irredundant facet and strict on every other facet. This gives distinct witnesses, and the own facet functional uniquely maximizes there within the finite witness list.

A convex combination with at least two distinct witnesses of positive weight strictly satisfies every facet inequality and belongs to A by convexity. Thus it lies in the excluded region if integral, even if the combination is on the relative boundary of the witness hull.

A same-parity pair would have an integral midpoint of that form. There are exactly 2^n parity classes, so saturation realizes each once. The argument covers a single facet and needs no boundedness of L.

overlap.comparison: Its finite-set Helly proof constructs strict witnesses relative to an exclusion system and proves the analogous hull property for that finite set. The present lemma starts with prescribed facets of a full-dimensional polyhedron and excludes all integer points of the witness hull via its convex domain A.

readability: The hull is empty in the lattice-polytope sense that its entire lattice trace consists of the listed vertices. No claim about lattice width enters the statement.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The given relative-interior witnesses are distinct exposed vertices of their hull, and every other point of that hull lies in the excluded interior region whenever it is integral.
